newsitem.title: USA: Ford sees 4,000 employees retiring early.
newsitem.headline: Ford sees 4,000 employees retiring early.

text.p: Ford Motor Co vice president David McCammon said Wednesday the automaker expects early retirement incentive programs to eliminate about 4,000 jobs, with more than half coming from Europe.
McCammon told a news conference here that the automaker has already started early retirement programs in the United States but still has more retirement incentives to announce in Europe.
Ford said earlier that it expects to take charges of $300 million to $400 million against its fourth quarter earnings to cover early retirement costs.

McCammon said the automaker also is planning other restructuring and cost reduction initiatives in its European automotive operations, where third quarter losses grew to $472 million from $320 million a year earlier.
Ford hopes to discuss those initiatives further by the time the automaker releases its fourth quarter results in January, McCammon said.
"We have work to do there and Brazil. Those are the two parts that we're not happy with," McCammon said.

A big part of Ford's efforts will be to reduce product costs in Europe to cope with a sluggish market that has led to high incentives. Ford's product development operations in Europe are centered in Dunton, England, and Merkenich, Germany, near Cologne.
"What's happening is there's overcapacity in Europe," McCammon said. "Everybody's fighting it out for market share and spending a lot of money" on incentives.
Ford reported that its consolidated third quarter profit rose to $686 million from $329 million a year earlier, but most of its profits again came from its Financial Services Group.
Automotive losses in Europe and Brazil held the company's automotive profits to $15 million, compared with a $201 million loss a year earlier.
